newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil continue downward slide.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil continue downward slide.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures extended losses on moderate mid-morning trade in what brokers' termed a "shakeout" of long positions build up in the recent rally.
At 0950 GMT, Dec Brent stood down 33 cents on the day at $23.74 a barrel while Nov gas oil was down $5.75 a tonne at $220.
As was the case on the way up, U.S. heating oil and IPE gas oil has been leading the complex lower. Brokers expected bigger losses when the NYMEX opened later on Thursday.
"We still have more to go. A good healthy shakeout after the high prices we have seen was needed. The funds have been really long so we have seen liquidation there," a gas oil broker said.
Dec Brent has shed nearly $1 since Tuesday's close while Nov gas oil has dropped more than $10 amid bearish reaction to big builds in heating oil stocks in the U.S. Northeast.
High productivity at European and U.S. refineries with a view to replenishing heating fuels stocks ahead of the winter has also taking some of the edge off the recent rally.
But brokers are stopping short of predicting a sharp price fall since it is too early to tell what the winter weather will mean to demand.
Despite the recent builds, U.S. and European heating oil stocks remain sharply below 1995 levels.

"We may have slowed down the pace but we are far from giving up on this rally. When winter hits in earnest in the first quarter (1997), we should be able to surpass the recent (post Gulf War) highs," a broker said.
News of a ceasefire among fighting Kurd factions in northern Iraq overnight also took some of the shine off the bullrun which last week took Brent to its highest level in nearly six years at $25.06.
